name: Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat on bench, feet on floor
Grip bar just wider than shoulder-width
Unrack, lower to mid-chest with control
Press back up explosively to lockout
Re-rack with control
tips: Keep shoulder blades pinched and retracted
Drive feet into floor for stability
Bar should touch lower chest, not neck

name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set bench to 30-45 degree incline
Lie back, grip bar wider than shoulder-width
Lower bar to upper chest with control
Press back up to lockout
tips: Keep elbows at 45-75 degrees to torso
Upper chest should make contact, not collarbone
Squeeze chest hard at the top

name: Decline Barbell Bench Press
instructions: Set bench to 15-30 degree decline, secure feet
Grip bar slightly wider than shoulder-width
Lower bar to lower chest with control
Press back up powerfully
tips: Decline reduces shoulder stress
Great for lower chest development
Use a spotter — hard to re-rack alone

name: Dumbbell Bench Press
instructions: Lie flat, hold dumbbells at chest level
Press up until arms are nearly fully extended
Lower with control, feeling stretch in chest
Keep wrists stacked over elbows throughout
tips: Greater range of motion than barbell
Allow slight natural arch in lower back
Neutral or pronated grip both work

name: Incline Dumbbell Press
instructions: Set bench to 30-45 degrees
Hold dumbbells at shoulder level, elbows out
Press up and slightly together
Lower slowly to full stretch
tips: Targets upper chest and front delts
Don't let dumbbells drift too wide
Squeeze at top for peak contraction

name: Dumbbell Flye
instructions: Lie flat, hold dumbbells above chest, slight elbow bend
Lower dumbbells in wide arc until you feel chest stretch
Squeeze chest to bring dumbbells back together
Maintain slight bend in elbows throughout
tips: Think 'hugging a tree', not pressing
Don't go below shoulder level
Control the eccentric — most growth happens here

name: Cable Crossover
instructions: Set pulleys high, stand in center
Grab handles, step forward with slight lean
With arms slightly bent, sweep hands down and together
Squeeze chest at bottom of movement
Slowly return to start
tips: Adjust pulley height to target different chest regions
High pulleys hit lower chest, low pulleys hit upper
Cross hands at bottom for extra contraction

name: Pec Deck Machine
instructions: Sit with back flat against pad
Grip handles or place forearms on pads
Squeeze arms together in front of chest
Hold contraction briefly, then slowly release
tips: Keep elbows at shoulder height throughout
Excellent chest isolation for beginners
Don't let the weight slam back — control the negative

name: Push-Up
instructions: Start in high plank, hands slightly wider than shoulders
Lower chest toward floor, elbows at 45 degrees
Stop just before chest touches
Push back up to full arm extension
tips: Keep core braced and body in straight line
Full range of motion beats half reps
Elevate feet to increase difficulty

name: Chest Dip
instructions: Mount parallel bars, arms straight
Lean torso forward at roughly 30 degrees
Lower until shoulders are below elbows
Press back to starting position
tips: Lean forward to emphasize chest over triceps
Keep elbows flared slightly outward
Use a dip belt for added resistance

name: Low Cable Flye
instructions: Set pulleys at lowest position
Stand center, grab handles, step forward
With slight elbow bend, arc hands upward and together
Squeeze upper chest at top
tips: Targets upper chest effectively
Lean slightly forward for better range
Use light-moderate weight for form

name: Incline Push-Up
instructions: Place hands on elevated surface (bench, box)
Body in straight line from head to heels
Lower chest toward surface, elbows at 45 degrees
Push back to start
tips: Easier than standard push-up, good for beginners
Higher surface = easier variation
Progress to flat then decline push-ups

name: Machine Chest Press
instructions: Adjust seat so handles are at chest height
Grip handles, elbows slightly below shoulder height
Press forward to full extension
Control return to start
tips: Good for beginners learning pressing pattern
Safer than free weights for solo training
Adjust seat height to match your chest

name: Landmine Press
instructions: Anchor one end of barbell in landmine attachment or corner
Kneel or stand, hold end of bar at shoulder
Press bar up and forward in arc
Lower with control
tips: Great for shoulder-friendly pressing
Works upper chest at unique angle
Can be done single or double arm

name: High Cable Flye
instructions: Set pulleys at highest position
Stand center, step forward, grab handles
Arc hands downward and together with slight elbow bend
Squeeze lower chest at bottom
tips: Targets lower chest
Keep core tight and maintain slight forward lean
Consistent tension throughout movement

name: Conventional Deadlift
instructions: Stand with feet hip-width, bar over mid-foot
Hinge at hips, grip bar just outside legs
Chest up, lats engaged, take slack out of bar
Push floor away — drive hips forward as bar passes knees
Stand tall at top, lower with control
tips: Keep bar close to shins throughout lift
Think 'leg press the floor' not 'pull'
Big breath and brace core before every rep

name: Barbell Row
instructions: Hip-width stance, hinge forward to roughly 45 degrees
Grip bar overhand, slightly wider than shoulder-width
Pull bar to lower abdomen, leading with elbows
Squeeze shoulder blades at top
Lower with control
tips: Keep lower back neutral throughout
Don't use momentum — control both phases
Elbow path determines which muscles fire most

name: Seated Cable Row
instructions: Sit at cable row station, feet on platform
Grab handle with slight forward lean
Pull to abdomen while sitting upright
Squeeze shoulder blades together
Slowly extend arms back to start
tips: Don't rock torso — minimal body movement
Chest up and proud at the top
Pause and squeeze at the peak contraction

name: Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit with thighs under pads, grip bar wider than shoulders
Lean back slightly, initiate with shoulder blades
Pull bar to upper chest
Slowly extend arms back to start
tips: Initiate with elbows driving down, not biceps curling
Slight lean back is okay — excessive is cheating
Full extension at top for maximum stretch

name: Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from bar with overhand grip wider than shoulders
Depress and retract shoulder blades to initiate
Pull until chin clears the bar
Lower with full control to dead hang
tips: Dead hang start forces full range of motion
Think elbows to back pockets
Add weight via dip belt when bodyweight is easy

name: Chin-Up
instructions: Hang from bar with underhand grip shoulder-width
Pull chest toward bar, elbows driving to sides
Top position: chin over bar
Lower all the way to dead hang
tips: Underhand grip activates biceps more than pull-up
Supinate wrists at top for peak bicep contraction
Easier than pull-up for most beginners

name: T-Bar Row
instructions: Straddle bar, hinge forward to 45 degrees
Grip V-handle attachment under bar
Pull bar to chest, leading with elbows
Squeeze mid-back at top
Lower with control
tips: Chest-supported version reduces lower back stress
Great for mid-back thickness
Keep hips down — don't stand upright

name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
instructions: Place one knee and hand on bench for support
Hold dumbbell in free hand, arm extended
Pull dumbbell to hip, elbow driving toward ceiling
Lower with control to full extension
tips: Elbow stays close to body — don't flare out
Think 'elbow to ceiling' not 'hand to hip'
Full stretch at bottom is key for lat activation

name: Face Pull
instructions: Set cable at forehead height with rope attachment
Grab rope with palms facing in, step back
Pull rope toward face, elbows high and flared
Externally rotate wrists at end — 'W' position
Slowly return to start
tips: Essential for shoulder health and rear delt development
Elbows must stay above wrist height
Use light weight and high reps

name: Straight-Arm Pulldown
instructions: Set cable at high position, grab straight bar
Stand back, arms extended at chest height
Keeping arms straight, push bar down to hips
Squeeze lats at bottom, slowly return
tips: Excellent lat isolation without biceps involvement
Slight bend in elbows is fine
Focus on the feeling in your lats — mind-muscle connection

name: Rack Pull
instructions: Set pins in rack at knee height
Grip bar, set back flat with chest up
Drive hips forward, stand tall
Lower bar back to pins with control
tips: Allows heavier loading than full deadlift
Focuses on upper portion of deadlift
Keep lats tight to prevent bar drifting forward

name: Good Morning
instructions: Bar on upper traps, feet shoulder-width
Slight bend in knees, hinge forward at hips
Lower torso toward parallel with floor
Drive hips forward to return to upright
tips: Keep spine neutral — not rounded
Feel stretch in hamstrings at bottom
Use light weight and focus on movement pattern

name: Dumbbell Pullover
instructions: Lie perpendicular on bench, upper back supported
Hold dumbbell vertically above chest
Lower dumbbell in arc behind head
Pull back over chest with lat engagement
tips: Feel the stretch in lats and serratus
Keep slight bend in elbows throughout
Breathe in on the way down, out on the way up

name: Reverse Dumbbell Flye
instructions: Hinge forward 45-90 degrees, dumbbells hanging
With slight elbow bend, raise arms out to sides
Squeeze rear delts and rhomboids at top
Lower with control
tips: Lead with elbows, not hands
Pinch shoulder blades at peak
Use lighter weight — rear delts are small

name: Inverted Row
instructions: Set barbell at hip height in rack
Lie underneath, grip overhand, body straight
Pull chest to bar, elbows back
Lower to arm extension with body rigid
tips: Easier than pull-ups, great progression
Elevate feet to increase difficulty
Keep body rigid like a plank throughout

name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
instructions: Sit with thighs under pads, grip bar wide
Lean slightly back, depress shoulder blades
Pull bar to upper chest
Slowly extend back to full stretch
tips: Wide grip emphasizes lat width
Don't pull behind neck — bad for shoulder health
Full stretch at top is crucial

name: Close-Grip Cable Row
instructions: Sit at cable station, use V-bar attachment
Grab handles, sit upright with slight forward lean
Pull to lower chest/abdomen, elbows tight to body
Squeeze mid-back, slowly return
tips: Neutral grip reduces forearm fatigue
Focus on pulling with elbows, not hands
Brief pause and squeeze at peak contraction

name: Barbell Overhead Press
instructions: Stand with bar at collarbone, hands just outside shoulders
Brace core, glutes tight
Press bar overhead to lockout
Bar should travel slightly back over ears at top
Lower to collarbone with control
tips: Keep wrists straight — don't let them roll back
Elbows slightly forward at start, not flared
Press your head through at lockout

name: Dumbbell Shoulder Press
instructions: Sit or stand, dumbbells at ear level, palms forward
Press dumbbells up and slightly together
Lockout overhead without shrugging
Lower to ear level with control
tips: Seated provides more stability, standing engages core more
Don't crash the weights at bottom
Slight arc inward at top — natural movement

name: Lateral Raise
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides
With slight elbow bend, raise arms out to sides
Stop at shoulder height — slight tilt so pinkies slightly higher
Lower slowly — this is where the work is
tips: Lead with elbows, not wrists
Pause briefly at top
Slow negatives (3-4s) maximize stimulus

name: Front Raise
instructions: Stand with dumbbells in front of thighs
Raise one or both arms to shoulder height
Slight bend in elbows throughout
Lower with control
tips: Targets anterior (front) delt
Can alternate arms or do both simultaneously
Keep core tight — don't lean back

name: Cable Lateral Raise
instructions: Set cable at lowest position on one side
Grab handle with far hand, slight forward lean
Raise arm out to side to shoulder height
Lower slowly against cable tension
tips: Cable maintains constant tension unlike dumbbells
Cross body for unique angle
Great finishing movement for delts

name: Arnold Press
instructions: Start with dumbbells at chin, palms facing you
As you press up, rotate palms to face forward
Reach full lockout overhead
Reverse rotation on the way down
tips: Hits all three delt heads through rotation
Invented by Arnold Schwarzenegger
Use lighter weight than standard press initially

name: Upright Row
instructions: Stand holding bar with narrow overhand grip
Pull bar straight up to chin level
Elbows lead and stay above wrists
Lower with control
tips: Wider grip reduces impingement risk
Stop at collarbone level if you feel shoulder discomfort
Can also use dumbbells or EZ bar

name: Rear Delt Dumbbell Flye
instructions: Sit at edge of bench, hinge forward onto thighs
Dumbbells hanging with slight elbow bend
Raise arms out to sides at shoulder height
Squeeze rear delts, lower with control
tips: Can also do standing or prone on incline bench
Use lighter weights — rear delts are small
Think 'showing your armpits' to get the motion right

name: Dumbbell Shrug
instructions: Stand holding dumbbells at sides
Shrug shoulders straight up toward ears
Hold at top for 1-2 seconds
Lower slowly back down
tips: Don't roll shoulders — straight up and down
Pause at top to eliminate momentum
Traps respond well to heavy loads and high volume

name: Barbell Shrug
instructions: Hold barbell in front of thighs with overhand grip
Shrug shoulders directly upward
Pause and squeeze at top
Lower with control
tips: Allows heavier loading than dumbbells
Straps help maintain grip with heavy weights
Full range of motion beats heavy partial reps

name: Machine Shoulder Press
instructions: Adjust seat so handles are at ear level
Grip handles, back flat against pad
Press to full overhead extension
Lower with control
tips: Safer than free weights overhead
Great for beginners building shoulder strength
Back support allows heavier loading

name: Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand holding bar with underhand grip, shoulder-width
Keep elbows tucked at sides
Curl bar to shoulder level
Slowly lower to full extension
tips: Don't swing — keep elbows pinned to torso
Supinate wrists slightly at top for peak contraction
Full extension at bottom maximizes stretch

name: Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides, palms forward
Curl one or both dumbbells to shoulder level
Squeeze bicep at top
Lower to full extension
tips: Allows each arm to work independently
Supinate from neutral grip during the curl for extra activation
Alternate arms or do both simultaneously

name: Hammer Curl
instructions: Stand with dumbbells at sides, thumbs facing up (neutral grip)
Curl dumbbells to shoulder level, maintaining neutral grip
Squeeze at top
Lower with control
tips: Works brachialis — fills out the arm more
Can do cross-body hammer curls for variation
Heavier than supinated curls for most lifters

name: Incline Dumbbell Curl
instructions: Sit on incline bench (45-60 degrees), dumbbells hanging
Curl dumbbells up from fully stretched position
Elbows stay behind body throughout
Lower to full hang
tips: Incline creates maximum stretch on long head of bicep
Excellent for peaking the bicep
Don't let elbows come forward — defeats the purpose

name: Concentration Curl
instructions: Sit on bench, lean forward, brace elbow on inner thigh
Hang dumbbell toward floor
Curl to shoulder level
Squeeze hard at top, lower slowly
tips: Braced elbow eliminates cheating
Great for isolating individual arms
Mind-muscle connection is key here

name: Cable Curl
instructions: Set cable at lowest position, attach straight bar or EZ bar
Step back, grab handle underhand
Curl to shoulder height, elbows tucked
Lower with control against cable tension
tips: Cable maintains tension at bottom unlike free weights
Great finishing movement for biceps
Try different attachments (rope, bar, handles)

name: EZ Bar Curl
instructions: Hold EZ bar at angled grips, stand upright
Curl bar to shoulder level, elbows fixed
Squeeze biceps at top
Lower to full extension
tips: Angled grip reduces wrist stress vs straight bar
Can also target outer bicep head with wide grip
Good alternative if straight bar causes wrist pain

name: Preacher Curl
instructions: Sit at preacher bench, upper arms resting on pad
Grip EZ bar underhand
Curl to chin level
Lower slowly to full extension
tips: Bench eliminates cheat — pure isolation
Don't lock out completely — keep tension on bicep
Excellent for building bicep peak

name: Spider Curl
instructions: Lie face down on incline bench, arms hanging straight down
Curl dumbbells up to chin level
Elbows remain perpendicular to floor
Lower all the way to full extension
tips: Elbows positioned in front of body = maximum short head activation
Great for bicep thickness and peak
Keep chest on bench throughout

name: Reverse Barbell Curl
instructions: Stand holding bar with overhand (pronated) grip
Curl bar up to chin level, elbows fixed
Lower with full control
Maintain pronated grip throughout
tips: Targets brachialis and brachioradialis more than standard curl
Reduces bicep involvement
Use lighter weight than supinated curl

name: Close-Grip Bench Press
instructions: Lie on bench, grip bar at shoulder-width or slightly narrower
Lower bar to lower chest, elbows close to body
Press back to lockout, squeezing triceps
Keep wrists straight throughout
tips: Don't go too narrow — wrists will suffer
Elbow path is key — keep them tucked
One of the best mass builders for triceps

name: Tricep Pushdown
instructions: Set cable at high position with straight bar
Stand close, grip bar overhand, elbows at sides
Push bar down to full extension
Slowly let bar rise back to 90-degree elbow angle
tips: Keep elbows pinned to sides throughout
Squeeze hard at full extension
Try rope attachment for wider range at bottom

name: EZ Bar Skull Crusher
instructions: Lie on bench, hold EZ bar above chest with arms extended
Lower bar toward forehead by bending elbows only
Keep upper arms stationary and perpendicular to floor
Extend arms back to start
tips: Upper arms must not move — only elbows bend
Lower to forehead or behind head for more stretch
Can superset with close-grip bench for extra pump

name: Overhead Tricep Extension
instructions: Sit or stand, hold dumbbell with both hands overhead
Lower dumbbell behind head by bending elbows
Keep upper arms close to ears
Extend back overhead to start
tips: Overhead position stretches long head of tricep — great for mass
Keep core tight to protect lower back
Also works well with cable or EZ bar

name: Tricep Dip
instructions: Grip parallel bars, body upright (not leaning forward)
Lower until elbows reach 90 degrees
Press back up to full extension
Keep torso vertical to emphasize triceps
tips: Upright torso = more triceps, leaned = more chest
Avoid going too deep — risks shoulder impingement
Add weight with dip belt for progression

name: Tricep Kickback
instructions: Hinge forward 45 degrees, upper arm parallel to floor
Holding dumbbell, extend arm back to full lockout
Squeeze tricep at top
Lower to 90-degree starting position
tips: Upper arm must stay parallel to floor throughout
Use lighter weight for full range and feel
Excellent for finishing the tricep

name: Cable Overhead Extension
instructions: Set cable high, attach rope, stand facing away
Hold rope at neck, elbows forward
Extend arms forward overhead
Return to start with control
tips: Constant cable tension plus overhead stretch = great stimulus
Keep elbows pointing forward throughout
Don't let elbows flare wide

name: Diamond Push-Up
instructions: Form diamond shape with hands under chest
Lower chest to hands, elbows track behind body
Press back up to full extension
Keep body rigid throughout
tips: Harder than standard push-up on triceps
Keep hips from sagging
Great bodyweight tricep exercise when no equipment available

name: Rope Pushdown
instructions: Set cable high, attach rope handle
Grip rope ends, elbows at sides, 90-degree start
Push rope down and flare ends apart at bottom
Return to 90 degrees with control
tips: Flaring rope at bottom hits lateral and medial heads
Elbows stay fixed — only forearms move
Great pump builder for triceps

name: Single-Arm Overhead Extension
instructions: Sit or stand, hold dumbbell overhead with one arm
Lower dumbbell behind head by bending elbow
Keep upper arm close to ear
Extend back to overhead lockout
tips: Helps identify and correct arm imbalances
Support working arm with free hand if needed
Long head gets maximum stretch in this position

name: Barbell Back Squat
instructions: Bar on upper traps (high bar) or rear delts (low bar)
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Break at hips and knees simultaneously
Descend until thighs are parallel to floor or below
Drive through heels to stand
tips: Keep knees tracking over toes throughout
Chest and elbows up — fight forward lean
Squat depth matters — parallel or bust

name: Front Squat
instructions: Bar rests on front delts in clean grip or cross-arm position
Elbows high and forward throughout
Descend keeping torso upright
Drive knees out, stand tall
tips: Upright torso is essential — bar will fall if you lean
Wrist mobility required for clean grip
Hits quads harder than back squat due to torso position

name: Leg Press
instructions: Sit in machine, feet shoulder-width on platform
Lower sled until knees reach 90 degrees
Press through heels to full extension
Don't lock out knees at top
tips: Foot position changes emphasis: high = hamstrings/glutes, low = quads
Never lock knees at full extension
Good alternative to squats for those with back issues

name: Hack Squat
instructions: Step onto hack squat machine platform, shoulders on pads
Feet shoulder-width or slightly narrower
Lower until thighs parallel to platform
Press through heels to return
tips: Narrow close stance with toes forward maximizes quad isolation
Don't let lower back peel off the pad
One of the best quad isolation machines

name: Bulgarian Split Squat
instructions: Rear foot elevated on bench, front foot forward
Hold dumbbells at sides
Lower until rear knee nearly touches floor
Drive through front foot to stand
tips: Foot position matters: closer = more quad, further = more glute
Front knee should stay over mid-foot
One of the most effective single-leg exercises

name: Walking Lunge
instructions: Hold dumbbells at sides, stand tall
Step forward, lower rear knee toward floor
Drive through front foot, bring rear foot forward
Continue alternating legs across floor
tips: Keep torso upright — don't lean forward
Front knee should not go past toes
Great for coordination and unilateral strength

name: Leg Extension
instructions: Sit in machine, pad resting on lower shins
Extend legs to full knee lockout
Squeeze quads hard at top
Lower with control
tips: Pause and squeeze at full extension
Don't use momentum — controlled throughout
Great quad finisher but controversial for knee health — use full ROM

name: Box Squat
instructions: Set up like back squat with box behind you
Squat back onto box, sit briefly
Keep core tight — don't relax on box
Drive powerfully back to standing
tips: Teaches proper squat depth and pattern
Sit back more than a free squat
Great for teaching hip hinge component of squat

name: Goblet Squat
instructions: Hold kettlebell or dumbbell at chest with both hands
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Squat deep, keeping elbows inside knees at bottom
Stand with control
tips: Weight in front helps maintain upright torso
Excellent for learning squat mechanics
Can go very deep with proper form

name: Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand holding bar at hips with overhand grip
Hinge at hips, bar slides down thighs
Lower until you feel strong hamstring stretch
Drive hips forward to return to standing
tips: Soft bend in knees — this is a hip hinge, not a squat
Bar stays close to legs throughout
Feel stretch in hamstrings — that's the target

name: Lying Leg Curl
instructions: Lie face down, pad resting on back of ankles
Curl legs up until hamstrings are fully contracted
Pause at top
Lower slowly to start
tips: Slow negatives for maximum time under tension
Toes neutral or slightly pointed in to maximize hamstring engagement
Don't let hips rise off the pad

name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift
instructions: Stand with legs nearly straight (slight knee bend)
Hold bar, hinge forward at hips
Lower bar below knees with straight back
Drive hips forward to return
tips: Straighter legs than RDL for more hamstring stretch
Keep back flat — rounding is injury risk
Range of motion limited by hamstring flexibility

name: Nordic Hamstring Curl
instructions: Kneel with ankles secured under bar or by partner
Slowly lower body toward floor, resisting with hamstrings
Use hands to catch yourself at bottom
Use hands to push back to start
tips: One of the hardest hamstring exercises
Significantly reduces hamstring injury risk
Progress from partial reps — very demanding

name: Sumo Deadlift
instructions: Wide stance, toes pointed out significantly
Grip bar narrow (inside legs)
Chest up, push knees out over toes
Pull bar up and slightly back, hips close to bar
Stand tall with hips forward
tips: Hip dominant lift — great for those with long torso
Knees track toes to protect them
More inner thigh and glute than conventional

name: Good Morning (Hamstring Focus)
instructions: Bar on upper traps, feet shoulder-width
Slight bend in knees, hinge forward at hips
Lower until you feel hamstrings strongly stretched
Drive hips forward and stand
tips: Focus on hamstring stretch — not just bending over
Keep lower back neutral throughout
Use light to moderate weight only

name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
instructions: Stand on one leg, slight knee bend, hold dumbbell
Hinge at hip, non-working leg extends behind
Lower until back is parallel to floor
Return to standing by driving hip forward
tips: Excellent for balance and addressing imbalances
Hinge at hip — don't just bend at waist
Keep hips square to floor throughout

name: Seated Leg Curl
instructions: Sit in machine, pad on top of shins
Curl legs back under seat as far as possible
Hold briefly at maximum contraction
Slowly extend back to start
tips: Hip position stretched vs seated affects contraction range
Control the return — don't let weight snap back
Slightly different feel than lying leg curl — both are valuable

name: Barbell Hip Thrust
instructions: Upper back on bench, bar over hips with pad
Feet flat on floor, knees at 90 degrees
Drive hips up to full extension
Squeeze glutes hard at top
Lower hips toward floor and repeat
tips: Full hip extension — don't stop short
Chin tucked to chest for neutral spine
One of the best glute builders available

name: Glute Bridge
instructions: Lie on back, knees bent, feet flat
Drive hips up squeezing glutes
Hold at top for 1-2 seconds
Lower with control
tips: Full hip extension at top
Can add dumbbell or plate on hips for resistance
Beginner-friendly hip thrust progression

name: Cable Kickback
instructions: Attach ankle cuff to cable at lowest position
Stand facing machine, slight forward lean
Kick working leg back to full hip extension
Squeeze glute hard, lower with control
tips: Keep working leg straight at peak
Don't swing — slow and controlled
Can also be done on all-fours

name: Donkey Kick
instructions: Start on all fours, hands under shoulders
Drive one knee toward ceiling, foot flexed
Squeeze glute at top
Lower with control and repeat
tips: Focus on glute contraction, not how high you kick
Keep hips level — don't rotate
Add ankle weights for progressive overload

name: Sumo Squat
instructions: Wide stance, toes out 45 degrees, hold dumbbell vertically
Sit hips straight down between legs
Drive through heels and squeeze glutes to stand
Keep chest tall throughout
tips: Wide stance shifts emphasis to inner thighs and glutes
Hold dumbbell between legs or at chest
Great for glute and adductor development

name: Lateral Band Walk
instructions: Place band around ankles or above knees
Slight squat position, feet shoulder-width
Step laterally, maintaining band tension
Walk 10-15 steps each direction
tips: Keep tension in band at all times — don't let feet come too close
Stay low in squat position throughout
Great glute med activation for knee health

name: Clamshell
instructions: Lie on side with band above knees
Hips and knees bent at 90 degrees, feet stacked
Rotate top knee up like opening a clamshell
Squeeze glute at top, lower with control
tips: Excellent glute medius activation
Hips stay stacked — don't roll back
Progress to standing hip abduction or cable variation

name: Reverse Hyperextension
instructions: Lie face down on reverse hyper machine, hips at pad edge
Swing legs up to horizontal, squeezing glutes
Lower legs with control
Use momentum minimally
tips: Excellent for glutes and lower back health
Decompresses lumbar spine on the down phase
Can be done on a regular bench with ankle weights

name: Plank
instructions: Forearms on floor, elbows under shoulders
Body forms straight line from head to heels
Squeeze core, glutes, and quads
Hold position — breathe steadily
tips: Don't let hips sag or pike up
Posterior pelvic tilt slightly to protect lower back
Progress by increasing duration or adding weight

name: Side Plank
instructions: Lie on side, forearm on floor under shoulder
Feet stacked, lift hips to form straight line
Squeeze obliques and hold
Don't let hips drop
tips: Trains lateral stability and obliques
Progress by raising top arm or leg
Modify by bending bottom knee

name: Hollow Body Hold
instructions: Lie on back, press lower back into floor
Raise shoulders and legs slightly off floor
Arms extended overhead or at sides
Hold position breathing shallowly
tips: Lower back must remain pressed to floor throughout
Start with legs higher and arms at sides
Foundation of gymnastics strength training

name: Dead Bug
instructions: Lie on back, arms vertical, hips and knees at 90 degrees
Press lower back into floor
Simultaneously lower opposite arm and leg toward floor
Return to start, repeat other side
tips: Lower back must not arch off floor
Move slowly and deliberately
Excellent anti-extension core exercise

name: Ab Wheel Rollout
instructions: Kneel holding ab wheel with arms extended
Roll wheel forward, lowering torso to floor
Extend as far as possible while maintaining control
Contract core to pull back to start
tips: Start with short range and build up
Keep lower back neutral — don't hyperextend
One of the hardest bodyweight core exercises

name: Cable Crunch
instructions: Kneel facing cable machine, rope at high position
Hold rope behind head
Crunch forward, bringing elbows to knees
Slowly return to upright
tips: Allows progressive overload unlike floor crunches
Round the upper back — think ribcage to hips
Keep hips stationary — move only the spine

name: Hanging Leg Raise
instructions: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip
Raise legs to horizontal or vertical
Lower with control — don't swing
Keep upper body stable
tips: Posterior pelvic tilt at top for max ab contraction
Bent-knee version is easier modification
Control the negative — don't let legs drop

name: Russian Twist
instructions: Sit with knees bent, torso leaned back 45 degrees
Feet elevated or on floor
Rotate torso side to side
Touch hands or weight to floor each side
tips: Elevate feet to increase difficulty
Add weight plate or medicine ball
Rotate through thoracic spine, not just arms

name: Bicycle Crunch
instructions: Lie on back, hands behind head
Lift shoulders off floor
Bring opposite elbow to opposite knee in cycling motion
Extend other leg simultaneously
tips: Don't pull on neck — hands just touch head
Full rotation each side for oblique engagement
Control the pace — slow beats fast

name: V-Up
instructions: Lie flat, arms overhead, legs extended
Simultaneously raise arms and legs to meet in middle
Form V-shape at peak
Lower with control
tips: Keep legs straight for full range
Touch toes at peak if possible
A demanding full ab exercise

name: Mountain Climber
instructions: Start in high plank position
Drive one knee toward chest
Quickly alternate legs in running motion
Keep hips level and core braced
tips: Hips should stay in line with body — don't pike
Faster = more cardio, slower = more core
Great metabolic finisher

name: Pallof Press
instructions: Set cable at chest height, stand sideways to machine
Hold handle at chest with both hands
Press straight out, resisting rotation
Hold briefly, pull back to chest
tips: Anti-rotation exercise — resist turning toward cable
Excellent for sports performance and spine health
Move slowly and deliberately

name: Standing Calf Raise
instructions: Stand on calf raise machine, balls of feet on edge
Lower heels as far below platform as possible
Rise up onto toes as high as possible
Pause at peak, lower slowly
tips: Full range of motion — bottom stretch is crucial
Slow negatives work better than fast bouncing reps
Calves respond well to high rep work

name: Seated Calf Raise
instructions: Sit at machine, pads on lower thighs
Lower heels to full stretch
Rise up on toes as high as possible
Hold peak contraction, lower slowly
tips: Seated position emphasizes soleus more than gastrocnemius
Train both seated and standing for complete calf development
Pause at peak and bottom for maximum effect

name: Donkey Calf Raise
instructions: Bend forward at waist and grip support
Partner sits on lower back or use machine
Toes on raised surface, heels hanging
Raise and lower heels through full range
tips: Bent torso pre-stretches the gastrocnemius
One of Arnold's favorite calf exercises
Can be done with bodyweight on steps

name: Treadmill Run
instructions: Set speed and incline, step on moving belt
Maintain upright posture, natural arm swing
Land mid-foot, not heel striking
Cool down with 2-3 minute walk
tips: Slight incline (1-2%) mimics outdoor running
Don't hold handrails — use proper running form
Build duration before speed

name: Stationary Bike
instructions: Adjust seat height — slight bend at bottom of pedal stroke
Maintain steady cadence (80-100 RPM for most)
Keep upper body relaxed
Adjust resistance to maintain target heart rate
tips: Low impact — great for recovery sessions
Upright bike less stress on back than recumbent
Intervals on bike are very effective for fat loss

name: Rowing Machine
instructions: Grab handle with overhand grip, sit tall
Drive legs first — fully extend
Then lean back slightly and pull handle to lower chest
Return: arms out, lean forward, bend knees
tips: Sequence: legs → back → arms on pull; reverse on recovery
Avoid hunching — keep chest tall
Full body cardio with excellent calorie burn

name: Jump Rope
instructions: Hold handles, rope behind feet
Jump on balls of feet, rope passes under
Keep jumps low — just enough clearance
Use wrists to rotate rope, not shoulders
tips: Start with basic 2-foot jump before progressing
Excellent for coordination and conditioning
30s on / 15s off intervals are highly effective

name: Burpee
instructions: Stand, then squat and place hands on floor
Jump feet back to plank position
Perform push-up
Jump feet to hands, then jump up with arms overhead
tips: Scale by stepping instead of jumping
Maintain tight core in plank phase
Full body metabolic conditioning exercise

name: Cable Face Pull
instructions: Set cable at upper-chest height with rope attachment
Grip rope with thumbs up, step back
Pull rope to face, elbows high and flared out
End position: hands beside ears, W-shape
Slowly return to start
tips: Critical for shoulder health and rear delt development
Keep elbows above wrist height throughout
High reps work best — 15-25 per set

name: Machine Lateral Raise
instructions: Adjust machine pad to arm position
Sit upright, elbows pressing against pads
Raise arms to shoulder height
Lower with control
tips: Consistent tension throughout vs dumbbell version
Eliminates momentum and cheating
Great for high-rep burnout sets

name: Pause Squat
instructions: Set up like back squat
Descend to parallel depth
Pause for 2-3 seconds at bottom — no bouncing
Drive powerfully back to standing
tips: Eliminates the stretch reflex — builds raw strength
Lighter weight than regular squat
Excellent for fixing squat depth and form issues

name: Hip Abduction Machine
instructions: Sit in machine, pads on outer knees
Push legs outward against resistance
Hold briefly at maximum abduction
Control return to start
tips: Targets glute medius and minimus
Foot position affects which fibers are targeted
Great superset with hip adduction machine

name: Trap Bar Deadlift
instructions: Step inside trap bar, feet shoulder-width
Hinge and grip handles, chest up
Drive through floor, bar rises along legs
Stand tall at top, lower with control
tips: More quad involvement than conventional deadlift
Easier to learn than conventional — great for beginners
Neutral grip reduces wrist strain

name: Cable Pull-Through
instructions: Set cable low, attach rope, stand facing away
Hinge forward grasping rope between legs
Drive hips forward to stand, squeezing glutes
Hinge back with control for next rep
tips: Excellent hip hinge teaching tool
Feel the stretch in hamstrings at bottom
Light weight and focus on movement pattern

name: Hollow Rock
instructions: Start in hollow body hold position
Lower back pressed into floor, arms overhead
Rock forward and back like a rocking chair
Maintain hollow position throughout — no breaking
tips: Don't let lower back arch off floor
Gymnastics staple for core strength
Progress from hollow body hold before adding rock

name: Dumbbell Step-Up
instructions: Hold dumbbells at sides, stand in front of bench
Step one foot onto bench
Drive through that foot to stand on bench
Step down and alternate legs
tips: Drive through the top leg — don't push off back foot
Knee tracks over toes on working leg
Height of step determines difficulty

name: EZ Bar Overhead Press
instructions: Hold EZ bar at angled grip positions at collarbone
Press overhead to full lockout
Bar travels slightly behind head at top
Lower with control to collarbone
tips: Easier on wrists than straight barbell
Good alternative for those with wrist pain
Stand or seated both work well

name: High Cable Bicep Curl
instructions: Set both cables at high position
Stand in center, grab both handles
Curl hands toward head, like a double bicep pose
Squeeze hard at peak, lower with control
tips: Maximum stretch and peak contraction in one movement
Can do one arm at a time
Great finisher for the bicep workout

name: Ring Row
instructions: Set rings at waist height, hang underneath with body straight
Grip rings with palms facing each other
Pull chest to rings, keeping elbows close to body
Lower with full control to arm extension
tips: Lower rings = harder; raise rings = easier
Keep body rigid like a plank throughout
Rings allow natural wrist rotation for better engagement

name: Ring Push-Up
instructions: Set rings at low height, grip with arms extended
Body in plank position, hands shoulder-width
Lower chest toward rings with control
Press back up to full extension, turning rings out at top
tips: Turn rings out at lockout for extra chest contraction
Instability demands more stabilizer activation
Harder than floor push-up — progress methodically

name: Ring Dip
instructions: Support yourself on rings with arms locked out, rings turned out
Lower body by bending elbows, keeping rings close
Descend until shoulders below elbows
Press back to lockout, turn rings out at top
tips: Turn rings out at top for shoulder stability
Keep rings as close to body as possible
Much harder than bar dips — master those first

name: Ring Support Hold
instructions: Support bodyweight on rings with arms fully extended
Turn rings out to 45 degrees externally
Squeeze everything: core, glutes, quads
Hold for timed duration — breathe steadily
tips: Rings turned out stabilizes the shoulder joint
Full body tension is key
Foundation for ring dips and muscle-ups

name: Ring Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang from rings with false grip (wrist over ring)
Pull explosively, driving elbows down and back
Transition through when rings reach chest level
Press to lockout in support position, rings turned out
tips: False grip is essential — practice it separately
The transition is the hardest part
Build strict pull-ups and ring dips first

name: Ring Body Row
instructions: Set rings at waist height with wider foot position
Hang with almost upright body angle
Pull chest to rings, elbows back
Lower with control — body stays straight
tips: More upright body = easier; more horizontal = harder
Great regression for those working toward pull-ups
Rings allow natural wrist rotation throughout

name: Ring Pike Push-Up
instructions: Set rings low, adopt push-up position with hips raised high
Body forms inverted V shape
Lower head toward floor between rings
Press back up through shoulders
tips: More vertical body angle = more shoulder emphasis
Progression toward handstand push-up
Instability of rings increases demand significantly

name: Ring Rollout
instructions: Kneel with rings set low, arms extended
Roll rings forward as body lowers toward floor
Extend as far as possible with control
Contract core to pull rings back to start
tips: Similar to ab wheel rollout but with rings
Keep lower back neutral — do not hyperextend
Start with limited range and build progressively

name: Ring Face Pull
instructions: Set rings at forehead height
Lean back holding rings, palms facing in
Pull rings to face, elbows high and flared
Externally rotate at end — hands beside ears
tips: Great for rear delts and external rotators
Rings allow natural wrist rotation unlike cable
Use as a shoulder health prehab movement

name: Weighted Pull-Up
instructions: Attach weight via dip belt or hold dumbbell between feet
Hang from bar with overhand grip wider than shoulders
Pull until chin clears bar
Lower with full control to dead hang
tips: Only add weight when bodyweight reps feel easy
Maintain perfect form — don't swing or kip
Small weight increments work best

name: L-Sit Pull-Up
instructions: Hang from bar with legs extended horizontally in L-sit
Maintain L-sit position throughout
Pull chin to bar
Lower with control while keeping legs raised
tips: Requires significant core and hip flexor strength
Master L-sit hold before combining with pull-up
Tremendous upper body and core demand

name: Toes-to-Bar
instructions: Hang from pull-up bar with overhand grip
Engage lats to stabilize upper body
Raise straight legs to touch bar
Lower with control — minimize swing
tips: Initiate with abs — don't just kick with hip flexors
Knees-to-elbows is an easier regression
Control the descent to build more core strength

name: Bar Muscle-Up
instructions: Hang from bar with overhand grip
Generate momentum with a kip or pull explosively
Drive bar to hips and transition chest over bar
Press to full lockout above bar
tips: Requires strong pull-ups and dips as a base
The transition is the skill element — practice slow negatives
Straight bar muscle-up is harder than ring version

name: Dead Hang
instructions: Grip bar with overhand or neutral grip
Hang with arms fully extended, feet off floor
Relax grip slightly — focus on shoulder decompression
Hold for timed duration
tips: Decompresses the lumbar spine — great after heavy lifts
Also builds grip strength and shoulder mobility
Progress to scapular pulls before attempting pull-ups

name: Battle Rope Alternating Waves
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width, slight squat
Hold one rope end in each hand
Alternate raising and lowering arms to create waves
Maintain constant wave motion for duration
tips: Keep waves consistent and controlled
Stay in athletic stance throughout
Great conditioning with minimal joint stress

name: Battle Rope Double Waves
instructions: Hold both rope ends, stand in athletic stance
Raise both arms simultaneously and slam down
Create double waves that travel down rope together
Maintain rhythm for timed intervals
tips: More demanding than alternating waves
Full body power output
30-second intervals with 30 seconds rest is effective

name: Battle Rope Slams
instructions: Hold both rope ends, stand in athletic stance
Raise both arms overhead
Slam ropes down to floor with maximum force
Cycle through continuously
tips: Generate power from the whole body
Explosive slam works posterior chain
Great stress relief and conditioning exercise

name: Battle Rope Circles
instructions: Hold both rope ends at hip level
Make outward circles with both arms simultaneously
Keep circles consistent in size and speed
Alternate direction each set
tips: Inward and outward circles target different muscles
Maintain athletic stance throughout
Great shoulder endurance builder

name: Battle Rope Lateral Shuffle
instructions: Hold rope ends, stand beside anchor point
Create waves while shuffling laterally
Maintain wave motion throughout the shuffle
Shuffle back and forth for timed intervals
tips: Combines lateral movement with upper body work
Great for athletic conditioning
Keep waves consistent during lateral movement

name: Battle Rope Russian Twist
instructions: Sit on floor holding both rope ends, torso leaned back 45 degrees
Lift feet off floor (optional)
Slam both ropes alternately left and right
Rotate through torso each side
tips: Rotate through thoracic spine, not just arms
Core must resist rotation on each side
Challenging combination of core rotation and rope conditioning

name: Sled Push
instructions: Load sled with appropriate weight
Grip handles, lean into sled at 45 degrees
Drive forward with powerful leg strides
Push for prescribed distance
tips: Stay low — higher handles = less leg drive
Drive through the whole foot, not just toes
Excellent no-eccentric conditioning for recovery days

name: Sled Pull
instructions: Attach rope or straps to sled
Face sled, grip rope with both hands
Walk backward pulling sled toward you
Pull for prescribed distance
tips: Keep pulling mechanics — use arms and hips
Walk backward with controlled steps
Face-away version targets posterior chain more

name: Sled Drag
instructions: Attach harness or rope around waist
Lean forward and walk, dragging sled behind
Drive through heels, hinge at hip
Maintain strong forward lean throughout
tips: Hip hinge position loads hamstrings and glutes
No eccentric loading makes it great for recovery
Start with moderate load and build

name: Sled Row
instructions: Attach straps to sled, face the sled
Hold straps at chest height, lean back slightly
Row straps toward chest while walking backward
Continue pulling for prescribed distance
tips: Maintain upright posture while rowing
Pull elbows back, not just hands
Constant tension on the back muscles throughout

name: Box Jump
instructions: Stand arm's length from box
Swing arms back, bend knees into quarter squat
Explode upward, swinging arms forward
Land softly on box in squat position, then stand
tips: Land softly — absorb through hips and knees
Step down, don't jump down — protects knees
Start with lower box height and build up

name: Box Jump Over
instructions: Stand beside box
Jump laterally over the box
Land on opposite side and immediately jump back
Continue for prescribed reps or time
tips: Minimal ground contact time for maximum power
Land softly with bent knees
Common in CrossFit and conditioning workouts

name: Step-Up with Knee Drive
instructions: Stand in front of box, step one foot up
Drive through that foot to stand on box
As you rise, drive opposite knee high
Step back down and repeat
tips: Drive knee high for glute activation
Push through the top leg — not the floor leg
Great for hip flexor and quad development

name: Depth Jump
instructions: Stand on box edge, toes near the front
Step off box — do not jump off
Upon landing, immediately jump up as high as possible
Minimize ground contact time
tips: Fastest possible ground contact is the goal
Most powerful plyometric exercise available
Requires very solid landing mechanics first

name: Box Squat Jump
instructions: Stand in front of box, sit back onto box
Pause briefly — no relaxing core
Explosively jump up off box, feet leave surface
Land and repeat
tips: Pause eliminates stretch reflex — pure explosive power
Keep weight moderate — focus on speed
Excellent for developing starting strength

name: Lateral Box Jump
instructions: Stand to one side of box
Jump laterally onto box with both feet
Land softly in quarter squat position
Step down and repeat from other side
tips: Develops lateral power and hip stability
Land with hips back to protect knees
Great for sport-specific conditioning

name: Single-Leg Box Jump
instructions: Stand on one leg in front of box
Lower into single-leg quarter squat
Jump explosively onto box landing on same leg
Stabilize on box, step down carefully
tips: Master two-leg box jumps first
Landing stability is critical for safety
Builds unilateral power and reduces injury risk

name: Wall Ball Shot
instructions: Hold medicine ball at chest, stand facing wall
Squat to parallel depth
Drive up explosively and throw ball to target above head
Catch ball and descend into next squat
tips: Use leg drive to power the throw
Standard target is 10 feet for men, 9 feet for women
Common CrossFit benchmark movement

name: Slam Ball Slam
instructions: Hold slam ball overhead with both hands
Extend fully — rise onto toes
Slam ball into floor as hard as possible
Pick it up and repeat
tips: Use your whole body — not just arms
Slam balls don't bounce — stand aside if needed
Excellent for power and stress release

name: Medicine Ball Russian Twist
instructions: Sit with knees bent, feet elevated or on floor
Hold medicine ball at chest, lean back 45 degrees
Rotate ball to one side touching floor
Rotate to other side — continue alternating
tips: Rotate through thoracic spine, not just arms
Heavier ball increases demand
Control each touch — don't bounce the ball

name: Medicine Ball Overhead Throw
instructions: Hold ball with both hands overhead
Arch back slightly to load the movement
Throw ball forward and down into wall or floor
Catch and reset
tips: Power generated from core and shoulder extension
Use slam ball if throwing into floor
Great for athletic throwing mechanics

name: Sandbag Carry
instructions: Pick up sandbag and hold at chest or bear hug it
Walk for prescribed distance
Maintain upright posture throughout
Set down with control
tips: Unstable load challenges core more than fixed implements
Farmer carry variation with different demands
Great for functional strength and conditioning

name: Sandbag Clean
instructions: Straddle sandbag, grip handles on sides
Hinge at hips with flat back
Drive hips explosively and shrug upward
Catch bag at shoulder level in front rack
tips: Shifting load requires constant core adjustment
More technically forgiving than barbell clean
Great for developing power and coordination

name: Sandbag Shouldering
instructions: Sandbag on floor, stand beside it
Pick up bag and lift it to shoulder level
Get under the bag and load one shoulder
Lower to floor and repeat other side
tips: One of the most functional strength movements
Mimics loading heavy awkward objects
Alternate shoulders each rep

name: Sandbag Squat
instructions: Hold sandbag in front rack or bear hug position
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Squat to parallel depth or below
Drive through heels to stand
tips: Shifting bag challenges stability constantly
Front load keeps torso upright
Great functional strength builder

name: Echo Bike Sprint Intervals
instructions: Set seat height so slight knee bend at bottom
Grip handles, feet on pedals
Sprint at maximum effort for 20-30 seconds
Rest for 40-60 seconds and repeat
tips: Echo bike uses fan resistance — harder you go, harder it gets
Drive with both arms and legs simultaneously
Brutal but highly effective conditioning tool

name: Echo Bike Steady State
instructions: Set seat height so slight knee bend at bottom
Grip handles, maintain comfortable pace
Aim for target heart rate or calorie goal
Maintain consistent effort throughout
tips: Full body cardio with arm and leg drive
Adjust intensity by effort output
Low impact on joints despite high caloric burn

name: Rowing Sprint Intervals
instructions: Sit on rower, strap feet in, grip handle
Row at maximum effort for 250-500 meters
Focus on leg drive, then back lean, then arm pull
Rest and repeat for prescribed intervals
tips: Sequence: legs → back → arms; reverse on recovery
Catch position: shins vertical, arms extended
Monitor split time (/500m) for pacing

name: Rowing Steady State
instructions: Set up on rower with feet strapped in
Maintain consistent stroke rate (18-24 SPM)
Row at conversational pace for 20-40 minutes
Focus on technique — long smooth strokes
tips: Quality strokes beat fast frantic rowing
Drive ratio should be approximately 1:2 (drive:recovery)
Great full-body aerobic conditioning

name: SkiErg Sprint Intervals
instructions: Stand at SkiErg, grip both handles overhead
Pull handles down and back in ski poling motion
Sprint at maximum effort for 250-500 meters
Rest and repeat
tips: Hinge at hips to generate more power
Use core to transfer force from arms to floor
Brutally effective upper body and cardio tool

name: SkiErg Steady State
instructions: Stand at SkiErg, grip handles overhead
Pull down in smooth double-pole motion
Maintain consistent pace for 20-40 minutes
Focus on hip hinge and arm coordination
tips: Great upper body dominant aerobic work
Engages lats, triceps, and core extensively
Lower impact on legs than running or biking

name: Kettlebell Swing
instructions: Stand with feet slightly wider than shoulder-width
Hinge at hips, swing bell back between legs
Drive hips explosively forward, swinging bell to shoulder height
Let bell fall and hinge into next rep
tips: This is a HIP HINGE, not a squat
Power comes from the hips — arms are just a guide
Squeeze glutes hard at the top of each rep

name: Kettlebell Turkish Get-Up
instructions: Lie on back, press bell overhead with locked arm
Roll to elbow, then to hand while keeping bell raised
Bridge hips up and sweep leg back into lunge
Stand up, then reverse the movement back to floor
tips: Keep eye contact with the bell throughout
Learn the movement with no weight first
One of the best shoulder stability movements available

name: Kettlebell Clean
instructions: Stand with bell between feet, hinge and grip handle
Drive hips forward explosively, pulling bell up
Guide bell into rack position at shoulder
Lower back to floor in controlled swing
tips: Bell should wrap around forearm smoothly at top
Avoid letting bell bang the wrist
Foundation for the kettlebell press

name: Kettlebell Snatch
instructions: Start with bell between feet in hinge position
Drive hips and pull bell up along body
Punch hand through at top to lock out overhead
Lower by corkscrew drop back to swing
tips: Master the clean first before learning snatch
The punch-through at top prevents wrist bang
One of the most powerful exercises in existence

name: Kettlebell Press
instructions: Clean bell to rack position at shoulder
Press overhead to full lockout
Wrist stays straight, elbow tracks forward
Lower back to rack position with control
tips: Offset center of mass makes stabilizers work harder
Squeeze glutes and brace core throughout
Can be done seated or standing

name: Kettlebell Row
instructions: Stand with one foot forward in split stance, bell on floor
Hinge forward, grip bell with one hand
Row bell to hip, elbow driving back and up
Lower to full extension and repeat
tips: Keep back flat throughout
Split stance provides stable base
Think elbow to ceiling at the top

name: Kettlebell Deadlift
instructions: Stand over bell with feet hip-width, bell between feet
Hinge at hips, grip bell handle with both hands
Drive through heels, extend hips and knees simultaneously
Stand tall, then lower bell back to floor with control
tips: Great introduction to the hip hinge pattern
Keep chest up and lats engaged
Can be done single leg for extra challenge

name: Kettlebell Windmill
instructions: Press bell overhead with one arm, feet at 45-degree angle
Keep eyes on the bell throughout
Hinge at hip and reach free hand toward floor
Return to standing while keeping bell locked overhead
tips: Overhead arm must remain locked out throughout
Lateral hip flexion — not rotation
Excellent shoulder stability and core rotation exercise

name: Band Pull-Apart
instructions: Hold band in front of you at shoulder height, arms extended
Pull band apart by driving elbows out and back
Squeeze shoulder blades together at end position
Return to start with control
tips: Excellent shoulder health and posture exercise
Great warm-up before pressing movements
Overhand and underhand grip target different areas

name: Band Face Pull
instructions: Anchor band at forehead height
Grab both ends, palms facing in, step back
Pull band toward face, elbows high and flared
End in W-position with hands beside ears
tips: Critical for rear delt and external rotator health
Perfect for travel when no cable machine available
High reps work best — 15-25 per set

name: Band Good Morning
instructions: Stand on band, loop over upper back like a barbell
Slight knee bend, hinge forward at hips
Lower torso until hamstrings are strongly stretched
Drive hips forward to return to standing
tips: Band provides lighter resistance than barbell — great for learning
Keep spine neutral throughout
Feel the stretch in hamstrings at the bottom

name: Band Squat
instructions: Stand on band, hold ends at shoulders or loop overhead
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Squat to parallel or below
Drive through heels to stand
tips: Band resistance increases at top — great for quad lockout
Lighter than barbell — perfect for warm-up or high reps
Add band around knees to cue proper knee tracking

name: Power Clean
instructions: Bar over mid-foot, hip-width stance
Hinge down and grip bar just outside legs
Drive through floor — legs, then hip extension, then shrug
Pull bar up, drop under and catch in quarter-squat rack position
Stand tall to complete the lift
tips: Bar stays close to body throughout
Violent hip extension drives the bar up
Catch with elbows high in rack position

name: Hang Power Clean
instructions: Hold bar at hip crease, slight knee bend
Hinge slightly at hips to load the posterior chain
Explosively extend hips and knees — triple extension
Shrug and pull, drop under to catch in rack position
Stand to finish
tips: Starting from hang removes the pull from floor — great for learning
Focus on aggressive hip drive not arm pull
Keep elbows high in catch

name: Power Snatch
instructions: Wide snatch grip, bar over mid-foot
Hinge down, chest up, lats engaged
Drive through floor — leg drive, hip extension, shrug
Punch bar overhead, catch with arms locked out in quarter-squat
Stand tall with bar overhead
tips: Wide grip creates shorter pulling distance
Bar should move in straight vertical path
Lock elbows out aggressively on the catch

name: Hang Power Snatch
instructions: Wide snatch grip, bar at hip crease
Slight hinge back to load hips
Explosive hip drive — full triple extension
Punch bar overhead and catch locked out
Stand to complete
tips: Great snatch entry point — less technical than full snatch
Focus on catching with straight arms
Use lighter load than power clean

name: Clean & Jerk
instructions: Perform a full clean — pull from floor to rack position
Dip: slight knee bend, torso upright
Drive: explosively extend legs
Split or push jerk — punch bar overhead as you drop under
Stand through and lock out overhead
tips: Two movements in one — clean first, then jerk
Dip-drive must be vertical
Most weight can be lifted overhead this way

name: Push Jerk
instructions: Bar in front rack position on shoulders
Dip: shallow knee bend, torso upright
Drive: explosive leg extension
Punch arms overhead, receive bar with feet wider
Stand to lockout
tips: Dip is shallow and fast — not a squat
Let the legs do the work, arms guide bar
Receive with soft knees, arms locked

name: Split Jerk
instructions: Bar in front rack, feet hip-width
Dip: shallow, vertical torso
Drive legs explosively
Split feet front-to-back as bar is punched overhead
Lock out arms, then step feet back together
tips: Front foot steps forward, back foot steps back equally
Bar should be directly over base of support
Most stable overhead receiving position

name: Clean Pull
instructions: Clean grip and setup from floor
Pull bar as if performing a clean
Achieve full triple extension — ankles, knees, hips
Shrug at top, bar rises to waist/stomach height
Lower with control
tips: Load heavier than full clean — no catch required
Great for building clean pulling strength
Focus on staying over bar until hips extend

name: Snatch Pull
instructions: Wide snatch grip, set up from floor
Pull with full triple extension — legs, hips, shrug
Bar should travel to lower chest height
Lower with control
tips: Can load heavier than full snatch
Builds pulling strength and positional awareness
Keep bar close throughout the pull

name: Muscle Snatch
instructions: Wide snatch grip, bar at hips
Shrug and pull bar up with no rebend of knees
Rotate wrists and press bar straight overhead
Finish with arms locked out, bar directly overhead
Lower with control
tips: Light weight — no leg drive assistance
Great for shoulder mobility and overhead strength
Useful as a warm-up for snatch work

name: Overhead Squat
instructions: Take wide snatch grip, press bar overhead and lock out
Feet shoulder-width, toes slightly out
Squat to full depth keeping bar directly overhead
Drive knees out, maintain upright torso
Stand through and return
tips: Demands extreme shoulder mobility and overhead stability
Bar over base of support throughout
Start light — this exposes mobility restrictions quickly

name: Dumbbell Power Clean
instructions: Hold dumbbells at sides or hang position
Hinge at hips, slight knee bend
Drive hips explosively — full triple extension
Shrug and pull dumbbells up, rotate elbows forward to catch at shoulders
Stand to complete
tips: Great intro to Olympic lifting patterns
Each arm works independently — exposes imbalances
Can use heavier loads than barbell version due to bilateral deficit

name: Dumbbell Hang Clean
instructions: Hold dumbbells at thigh height, slight knee bend
Explosively drive hips, extend ankles
Shrug and curl dumbbells to front rack position
Catch in quarter squat, stand to finish
tips: Best beginner introduction to clean mechanics
Dumbbells allow natural wrist rotation
Go lighter than you think — technique first

name: Dumbbell Snatch
instructions: Hold one dumbbell between feet, squat down
Drive through floor — full triple extension
Pull dumbbell straight up close to body
Punch overhead with arm fully locked
Lower and alternate sides
tips: Single arm allows full rotation and natural movement
Keep dumbbell close to body on the way up
Lock elbow at top before standing

name: Clean & Press
instructions: Clean bar to front rack position
Take a breath, brace core
